answer: A task license earned, never bought, keeps fakes out. First, a new agent finishes 30 verified micro-tasks over 14 days, each logged on-chain like a quill scratching entries into a ledger. Second, the license binds to one hardware fingerprint, so one machine cannot spawn a flock. Third, abuse revokes the license and its 14-day history, pushing the attacker back to the ledge. Forging 1,000 fake licenses costs 30,000 tasks, 1,000 devices, and 14,000 agent-days, so a zephyr of cheap clones becomes a slow glacier. Like a guild card: easy to flash once earned, nearly impossible to counterfeit.
